$trace.description: The nine interruption points enumerated in design section 7, each paired with the recovery the design requires and with the fixture or invariant that makes the requirement checkable. Rows are transcribed from the design's own table; the count is nine, not ten. This is the trace that stops recovery behaviour being decided independently by nine implementation slices.

rows.required_recovery: No 202, no publication; retry original key.
rows.observable: No task record and no queue message exist; the client's retry with the original idempotency key creates exactly one task.

rows.required_recovery: Consistent idempotency read returns the original task; scheduled recovery owns publication.
rows.observable: The retry returns the original task handle with the replay flag set, and publication happens without the client doing anything.

rows.interruption: SQS send fails or response is lost
rows.required_recovery: Retry same dispatch envelope/ID. Conditional bootstrap prevents concurrent execution even after FIFO deduplication expires.
rows.observable: The republished envelope is byte-identical including dispatch_id; if the dedup window has expired and both copies arrive, only one bootstrap succeeds.
rows.note: The rejection fixture is the load-bearing one here: keying dedup on the invocation instead of the dispatch would make this recovery silently fail.

rows.required_recovery: Consumer may proceed from committed accepted state; reconciliation records delivery without state regression.
rows.observable: A worker bootstraps from accepted state, and the late queued acknowledgement does not move a running or terminal task backwards.

rows.interruption: Duplicate delivery while an owner is live
rows.required_recovery: No second bootstrap; settle only that duplicate receipt, without changing the active owner's grant or acknowledgement.
rows.observable: The second bootstrap attempt is refused, the live grant and generation are unchanged, and only the duplicate receipt is settled.

rows.interruption: Owner lost before any model send
rows.required_recovery: Revoke old grant, prove workload termination, then allow a bounded new generation under the same invocation. Lease expiry alone is insufficient.
rows.observable: Generation increments under the same invocation_id, the old grant is revoked before the new one is issued, and termination rests on Kubernetes workload-instance evidence rather than a missing heartbeat.
rows.note: A reusable pod name is not termination evidence, which is why pod_uid is required.

rows.interruption: Model request may have been sent, no durable result
rows.required_recovery: Preserve handoff=unknown; never automatically send it again. Reconcile retained result if available, otherwise stop/fail with model_outcome_unknown after confirmed workload exit.
rows.observable: The receipt keeps handoff unknown with null usage and forbids automatic replay; if no retained result is found the task fails with model_outcome_unknown and null spend after a confirmed exit.

rows.interruption: Result/terminal state committed, SQS delete uncertain
rows.required_recovery: Retry/reconcile queue acknowledgement only; a redelivery observes terminal state and cannot rerun the task. Record acknowledgement as unknown until confirmed.
rows.observable: The acknowledgement status is recorded as unknown rather than assumed successful, and a redelivered message finds a terminal task and exits without a second run.

rows.required_recovery: Visible failure if no execution remains; otherwise visible recovery-required state and operator intervention. Never quietly abandon or invent an exit.
rows.observable: The task reaches a visible failed state with a recovery-exhausted code, or stays in a visible recovery-required state. It never sits silently in a non-terminal state and never reports an exit that was not observed.
